title: ¿Qué tal?
blurbEn: A short conversation. Here you meet 'estar', the second Spanish verb for 'to be' — the one used for how someone feels.
body:
—Hola, Ana. ¿Qué tal estás?

—Muy bien, gracias. ¿Y tú?

—Hoy estoy un poco cansada.

—¿Por qué?

—Porque trabajo mucho.

—Adiós, Ana.
translationEn:
"Hello, Ana. How are you?"

"Very well, thank you. And you?"

"Today I am a little tired."

"Why?"

"Because I work a lot."

"Goodbye, Ana."

estás.note: From 'estar', not 'ser'. Feelings and moods use 'estar'.

cansada.note: Ends in -a because Ana is female.

phrases.note: The everyday greeting. '¿Qué tal?' on its own works too.
Two words with an accent. Written as one word without an accent, 'porque', it means 'because'.
